Neither sync-opencode-edition.js --check nor sync-kimi-edition.js --check runs in any of the four chains; both live only under npm run test:kaola-workflow:editions, which is in neither npm test nor the full tier. Measured: after editing three routing skeletons, generate-routing-surfaces --check reported all 18 tracked surfaces byte-matching at exit 0 while every one of the six edition trees still carried the old wording, and only an explicit six-invocation sync propagated it. The same run also found the four gitlab/gitea edition trees already stale against e4522be9, because install-all.sh --forge=github regenerates the github trees only; that drift had been sitting green until the run regenerated it incidentally. The trees are gitignored, so neither git status nor a diff review surfaces the staleness either. These are consumer-facing surfaces — the prose an opencode or kimi user actually reads — and the failure is silent in both directions, since each tree stays self-consistent and its own suite passes once someone finally runs it. SPECIFY THE RESULT, NOT THE MECHANISM: the wanted outcome is that a skeleton edit cannot reach a green four-chain receipt while an edition tree still carries the old prose; whether that is adding the two --checks to the chains, folding them into generate-routing-surfaces --check, or something else is the implementer's call, as is whether the check belongs in every chain or only where the diff touches templates/routing/. Note the neighbouring asymmetry already on ADR 0017's watch list: opencode is the edition missing a remediation guard its kimi sibling has. |
| #970 | A mission-list item can carry a result while still reading in-flight, and the run archives silently | open | issue-970 | Observed with a count, not derived — the #968 run archived with 7 of 17 items carrying a result and still reading status: in-flight, while the run itself was complete (four chains green, walkthrough 209/209, issue closed, sink clean). Cause was the third write moment happening by halves: outcomes written with edits whose match string omitted the status line, then patched around twice by inventing a status_note field, which put three non-spec field names into the durable record (status_note, result so far, earlier result). That record is repaired in a follow-up commit; the class is what this issue is about. Severity comes from the resume rule, not from tidiness: mission-list.md is the artifact a successor reads first, in-flight items are documented as the only decision to make, and an item reading in-flight WHILE carrying its own result inverts "look for the work, not the worker" — a successor re-dispatches finished work, and the result line that would correct it is the line the rule does not send it to. The archive is read as evidence by later runs, so the damage outlives its run. DO NOT BUILD A GATE: the record is deliberately not attested, not frozen and not machine-verified, stated as intentional in CLAUDE.md and ADR 0017, and a refusal would be a mechanism justified by "the agent might get this wrong". What changed is only that it stopped being might. SPECIFY THE RESULT: at finalize, a run whose record shows an item with an outcome but a non-done status is TOLD so — the same measure-and-report shape finalize already uses for the chain receipt and changed paths, landing on the envelope and in finalization-summary.md, with no refusal and no new required field. Whether that lives in the finalize transaction, the gap sweep, or elsewhere is the implementer's call. One correctness note for whoever takes it: the condition is outcome-present-and-status-not-done, NOT status-is-in-flight — a genuinely in-flight item with no result at finalize is a different and louder problem, and conflating them makes the report useless exactly where it matters. |

The surface leads you into it: worktrees are on by default, Step 4 has you resolve ACTIVE_WORKTREE_PATH and establishes the worktree as the phase's working location, Step 10 wraps its command in (cd "$ACTIVE_WORKTREE_PATH" && ...) twice because the transaction genuinely must run there, and Step 7 carries NO cwd guidance at all — measured, a scan of the whole Step 7 block for cd/main/worktree/root returns nothing. Ordering disguises it as intermittent: after Step 10 mirrors the folder into the worktree the same command succeeds, so a run that swept gaps late would never see it. SPECIFY THE RESULT: the sweep resolves the run folder the way the rest of finalize does — against the authority folder — or the surface says plainly which tree to run it from. Unspecified whether that is root resolution inside kaola-workflow-gap-sweep.js, reuse of the main-root resolution the finalize transaction already performs, or a one-line cwd note; note the surface is GENERATED, so a prose fix belongs in templates/routing/finalize.skeleton.md and reaches 6 tracked plus 6 edition surfaces, never a rendered surface. Low severity — it costs a confused minute, not correctness, and the sweep refuses loudly rather than passing vacuously; filed because "the artifact is missing" is a misleading thing to be told when the artifact exists. |

## Rules

- A separate roadmap/research session owns discovering and adding future work to GitHub issues.
- `workflow-next` fetches GitHub issues and mirrors active implementation work here.
- After each `workflow-next` cycle, refresh this file from issue state.
- Move completed workflow project folders to `kaola-workflow/archive/`.
- Close linked GitHub issues only after acceptance criteria pass.
- Keep commit and push as the final Finalization step after docs, issues, roadmap, archive, and metadata are complete.

### Project rules
## The design — read `docs/decisions/0017-the-mission-list.md` first

**The derivation is finished and the owner has ruled.** The work is now **build ADR 0017**.
ADR 0016 is its predecessor and still worth reading, but where the two disagree, 0017 wins.

### The premise

The workflow was built when agents were weak orchestrators, so it encoded orchestration **as
constraint**. That premise expired, and 0017 acts on the consequence 0016 stopped short of: if the
agent orchestrates itself, the plan need not be a machine-readable schedule.

**The existence proof is observed, not argued.** A bare session — no framework, no plan, no gates, no
bookkeeping, given only the main-orchestrator role plus a goal — decomposed the work, ran six
concurrent subagents across disjoint files with no conflicts, found real defects, and did not drift.

### What the design is

**One file per run. Four fields per item — `item` / `status` / `dispatched` / `result` — written at
three moments** (created, dispatched, closed), plus a header line carrying the goal. No script is
required; a file convention suffices. An item is a mission in one line of prose: hints and facts,
never a prescription. Tools are what the orchestrator already reaches for — subagents, worktrees —
offered and declinable.

### The governing rule for every change

> **Derive ADDITIVELY. Add only what an observed failure demands. Silence is an answer.**

Subtractive derivation asks *"may I remove this?"*, and there is always an answer that keeps it —
three separate passes of the 0017 discussion preserved machinery under *"harder to reason about"*
dressed as *"permits irreversible harm"*. Additive derivation asks *"what forced this to exist?"*

0016's **delete the verdict, keep the measurement** still governs anything that survives.

### Nothing refuses

The refusal count is **zero**. R1 was never armable, the consent valve is the orchestrator asking the
user, and R3 is now a report.

**Concurrency carries no machinery at all** — no antichain sweep, no disjointness check, no
serializer taxonomy, no evidence line, no caps. Disjointness is the agent's call, with no inspection.

### Owner rulings — do not re-litigate

- **The sink reports; the orchestrator owns the outcome.** *Supersedes the 2026-07-29 "R3 survives
  permanently" ruling.* The sink says what it found; the orchestrator gets the branch right — correct
  merge, resynchronize, or **file a PR** — and cleans up after. The change is not refuse-versus-proceed;
  it is **who is accountable for the branch ending up right.**
- **Any form of regulation or structure is limiting.** A mechanism justified by *"the agent might get
  this wrong"* argues against the design's premise rather than for a gate.
- **Do not over-complicate. There is already too much in this project.**
- **No run-cost ledger is built.** *(Stands from 2026-07-29.)* Residual risk accepted: if it recurs,
  it recurs silently.

### Watch-list discipline

Mechanisms derived for failure classes **never observed** in this methodology are recorded, not
built — see `docs/decisions/0017-the-mission-list.md` § *The watch list*. Each row names the
observation that would arm it, and a row whose mechanism was built and later removed names the commit
to recover it from. **Do not build one speculatively.**

### Working rules that survive

- **The unit of progress is a MECHANISM removed. Never a test removed.** Tests fall out with the
  mechanism.
- **A tool the agent is forced to use is a gate wearing a tool's name.** Test: can the agent decline
  it and still finish?
- **Correctness is never traded for the count.** A defect found while cutting gets fixed even when
  the fix adds code.
- **Premises get measured before they get built on.** A premise that collapses is the result, not a
  setback — and this cuts both ways. Two capability claims in the corpus turned out to be untraced:
  #854 row 9's *"every traced run silently serialized"* is a **tooling** defect (`open-next`
  single-opened a frontier the planner had authored as parallel), and 0016's *"a missing reviewer
  produces a merge"* cites no trace at all.
- **Grade against driven behaviour, never the condition census.** It is a sound ratchet and an index
  of emission sites. It is not a population.
- **Convergence is weaker evidence than it looks. Prefer the disagreements.**
